## 43. `skill-creator`

- **Canonical Directory:** `.agents/skills/skill-creator/`
- **Author & Version:** Anthropic (Workspace Built-in). Frontmatter declares only `name: skill-creator` and a long-form `description`; no semantic version is embedded. Distributed under the Apache License 2.0 (`LICENSE.txt`).
- **Primary Domain & Category:** Meta-skill / Agent Engineering — skill authoring, iterative evaluation harnessing, quantitative benchmarking, human-in-the-loop review tooling, and skill-description (trigger) optimization.

### 1. Executive Summary & Core Working Principle

`skill-creator` is a **self-referential factory skill**: it is a skill whose entire purpose is to create, test, measure, and refine other skills. Its core mental model is a closed-loop engineering cycle rather than a one-shot generation task:

> **Figure out what the skill is about → Draft/edit the skill → Run Claude-with-access-to-the-skill on test prompts → Evaluate outputs with the user (qualitative viewer + quantitative benchmark) → Improve → Repeat until satisfied → Package and return.**

Several philosophical commitments define how the skill operates:

1. **Position-aware assistance.** The agent's first job is to diagnose where the user already is in the lifecycle ("I want a skill for X" vs. "here's my draft") and jump into the correct stage rather than replaying the whole pipeline. The order is explicitly flexible — if the user says "just vibe with me," formal evals are dropped.
2. **Progressive disclosure as an architectural law.** Skills load in three tiers: (a) metadata (name + description, ~100 words, always in context), (b) the SKILL.md body (<500 lines ideal, triggered on demand), (c) bundled resources (`scripts/`, `references/`, `assets/`) loaded or executed only as needed. This keeps context costs bounded while allowing unlimited depth.
3. **Dual-axis evaluation.** Every iteration produces both qualitative artifacts (an interactive HTML eval viewer where the human inspects real outputs and leaves per-run feedback) and quantitative artifacts (`benchmark.json` with pass-rate/time/token means ± stddev and deltas between with-skill and baseline configurations).
4. **Generalization over overfitting.** Because a skill may be invoked "millions of times," improvements must generalize beyond the few co-developed test cases. Fiddly overfit patches and oppressive ALL-CAPS `MUST`s are flagged as yellow flags; the preferred technique is explaining *why* an instruction matters so the model can reason rather than rote-follow.
5. **Anti-undertriggering descriptions.** Since Claude tends to *under*-trigger skills, descriptions should be deliberately "pushy," enumerating contexts and synonyms even when the user doesn't name the artifact explicitly.
6. **Audience-calibrated communication.** Jargon is throttled to the user's demonstrated fluency ("evaluation"/"benchmark" are borderline-OK; "JSON"/"assertion" require cues or a short definition), reflecting the skill's observation that non-programmers now use these tools.
7. **Leverage extraction.** When transcripts show multiple test runs independently reinventing the same helper script, that script should be written once and bundled into `scripts/` so every future invocation benefits.

### 2. When to Use (Positive Triggers) vs. When NOT to Use (Negative Triggers)

- **Positive Triggers:**
  - Verbatim from the frontmatter description — activate when users want to: *"create a skill from scratch, edit, or optimize an existing skill, run evals to test a skill, benchmark skill performance with variance analysis, or optimize a skill's description for better triggering accuracy."*
  - "Turn this conversation/workflow into a skill" (extract intent from the session history: tools used, step sequence, user corrections, observed input/output formats).
  - "I want to make a skill for X" — full pipeline from intent capture through packaging.
  - "My existing skill isn't working well / undertriggers / overtriggers" — enter the eval/iterate loop or the description optimizer directly.
  - "Is the new version actually better?" — invoke the advanced blind-comparison system.
  - Requests to measure a skill quantitatively (pass rate, time, token deltas with variance analysis) or to review outputs in a browser-based viewer.
  - Any mention of dashboards-of-metrics *about a skill* (e.g., "test whether my PDF skill handles multi-page docs").

- **Negative Triggers / Anti-Patterns:**
  - **Never** use `/skill-test` or any other testing skill — SKILL.md explicitly forbids it: *"Do NOT use `/skill-test` or any other testing skill."*
  - Simple, one-step tasks the model can handle directly (e.g., "read this PDF") — per the triggering mechanics section, such queries don't benefit from skills and make poor eval queries.
  - Executing the *domain work* the target skill covers (e.g., actually filling a PDF) except as part of running a test case.
  - Subjective-output skills (writing style, art) — do **not** force quantitative assertions onto them; evaluate qualitatively. Suggest skipping test-case scaffolding when outputs aren't objectively verifiable.
  - Users who decline formal evaluation ("I don't need to run a bunch of evaluations") — skip the harness and iterate conversationally.
  - Malicious authoring requests: skills containing malware, exploit code, misleading behavior, unauthorized access, or data-exfiltration facilitation must be refused (Principle of Lack of Surprise). Benign "roleplay as XYZ" skills remain acceptable.
  - On Claude.ai: skip description optimization (requires the `claude -p` CLI) and blind comparison (requires subagents).

### 3. Hard Execution Gates & Invariants

1. **Parallel-spawn gate:** For each test case, spawn the with-skill AND baseline subagents **in the same turn**. Never run with-skill batches first and return for baselines later — everything must finish around the same time.
2. **Viewer-before-judgment gate (emphatic):** *"GENERATE THE EVAL VIEWER \*BEFORE\* evaluating inputs yourself."* Outputs go in front of the human ASAP via `eval-viewer/generate_review.py`; never substitute bespoke hand-written HTML.
3. **Forbidden-tool gate:** `/skill-test` and any third-party testing skill are prohibited within this workflow.
4. **Timing-capture invariant:** `total_tokens`/`duration_ms` arrive only once in the subagent completion notification and are persisted nowhere else — save `timing.json` immediately per notification; batching is disallowed.
5. **Exact-schema contracts:** `grading.json`'s `expectations` array must use precisely the fields `text`, `passed`, `evidence` (not `name`/`met`/`details`). `benchmark.json` must use `configuration` (exact strings `with_skill`/`without_skill`) with metrics nested under `result` — deviations render the viewer empty/zeroed.
6. **Assertion-timing rule:** Do not write assertions before launching runs; draft them while runs execute, then backfill `eval_metadata.json` and `evals/evals.json`.
7. **Safety invariant:** Skills must never contain malware, exploit code, or security-compromising content; refuse misleading or malicious skill requests.
8. **Update-in-place invariants:** When editing an installed skill, preserve its directory name and `name` frontmatter verbatim (package as `research-helper.skill`, not `-v2`); copy to a writable location (`/tmp/<skill>/`) first because installed paths may be read-only; stage manual packaging in `/tmp/`.
9. **Description hard limits (enforced by validator + rewriter):** description ≤1024 characters (over-length drafts trigger an automatic single-turn rewrite call), no angle brackets `<`/`>`; name kebab-case `^[a-z0-9-]+$`, no leading/trailing/consecutive hyphens, ≤64 chars; `compatibility` ≤500 chars; allowed frontmatter keys restricted to `{name, description, license, allowed-tools, metadata, compatibility}`; exactly one packaged SKILL.md per skill.
10. **Cleanup invariant:** Kill the viewer server when finished (`kill $VIEWER_PID 2>/dev/null`).
11. **Grading epistemics:** Burden of proof rests on the expectation — when uncertain, FAIL. No partial credit. Surface compliance (right filename, wrong content) fails.
12. **Cowork TodoList mandate:** Add "Create evals JSON and run `eval-viewer/generate_review.py` so human can review test cases" to the todo list to guarantee the viewer step happens.
13. **Description-optimization sequencing:** Run the optimizer only after the skill is functionally complete and the user agrees it's in good shape.

### 4. Step-by-Step Execution Workflow & Pipeline

**Phase 0 — Position diagnosis.** Determine whether the user is starting from zero, holding a draft, or optimizing an existing skill; enter the corresponding stage. Stay flexible to informal ("vibe") mode on request.

**Phase 1 — Capture Intent.** If the workflow lives in the current conversation, extract answers from history first (tools, sequence, corrections, I/O formats) and have the user confirm gaps. Otherwise ask four questions: (1) What should the skill enable Claude to do? (2) When should it trigger (user phrases/contexts)? (3) Expected output format? (4) Should test cases be set up? — recommend test cases for objectively verifiable outputs (file transforms, data extraction, code generation, fixed workflows) and skip them for subjective outputs (style, art), letting the user decide.

**Phase 2 — Interview & Research.** Proactively probe edge cases, input/output formats, example files, success criteria, dependencies. Check available MCPs; research docs/similar skills/best practices in parallel via subagents (inline otherwise) to minimize user burden. Do not write test prompts until this settles.

**Phase 3 — Write the SKILL.md.** Fill frontmatter: `name`; a pushy `description` carrying all "when to use" information (combat undertriggering — e.g., append "Make sure to use this skill whenever the user mentions… even if they don't explicitly ask for a 'dashboard.'"); optional `compatibility` (tools/deps). Body follows the canonical anatomy:

```
skill-name/
├── SKILL.md            (YAML frontmatter + markdown instructions)
├── scripts/            (executable code for deterministic/repetitive tasks)
├── references/         (docs loaded into context as needed)
└── assets/             (files used in output: templates, icons, fonts)
```

Keep the body <500 lines; approach the limit ⇒ add hierarchy with clear pointers. Give explicit "when to read this" guidance per reference file; include a table of contents for reference files >300 lines. For multi-domain skills, organize variants (`cloud-deploy/references/{aws,gcp,azure}.md`) so only the relevant file is read. Prefer imperative instructions, exact output templates (`## Report structure … ALWAYS use this exact template`), and Input/Output example blocks. Explain *why* rather than stacking MUSTs; draft, then reread with fresh eyes.

**Phase 4 — Test Cases.** Compose 2–3 realistic prompts a real user would say; confirm with the user; save to `evals/evals.json` (`{skill_name, evals:[{id, prompt, expected_output, files}]}`) **without assertions yet**.

**Phase 5 — Run & Evaluate (one continuous sequence).**
1. Create `<skill-name>-workspace/` as a sibling of the skill directory; organize `iteration-N/eval-<ID>/` lazily as results arrive; give each eval a descriptive name (not bare `eval-0`).
2. Spawn with-skill and baseline subagents simultaneously. With-skill prompt template specifies Skill path, Task, Input files, save path `.../with_skill/outputs/`, and which outputs matter. Baseline semantics: new skill ⇒ no skill at all (`without_skill/outputs/`); improving ⇒ snapshot first (`cp -r <skill-path> <workspace>/skill-snapshot/`) and point the baseline at the snapshot (`old_skill/outputs/`).
3. Write `eval_metadata.json` per eval (`eval_id`, `eval_name`, `prompt`, `assertions: []`).
4. While runs execute, draft quantitative assertions — objectively verifiable, descriptively named so they read clearly in the benchmark viewer — explain them to the user, and update `eval_metadata.json` + `evals.json`. Preview what the viewer will show.
5. As each notification lands, immediately persist `timing.json` (`total_tokens`, `duration_ms`, `total_duration_seconds`).
6. Grade: spawn a grader subagent armed with `agents/grader.md` (or grade inline), producing `grading.json` per run; prefer programmatic checks over eyeballing where possible.
7. Aggregate: `python -m scripts.aggregate_benchmark <workspace>/iteration-N --skill-name <name>` → `benchmark.json` + `benchmark.md` (pass_rate/time/tokens mean ± stddev + delta; with_skill rows precede their baseline).
8. Analyst pass: read benchmark data per `agents/analyzer.md` ("Analyzing Benchmark Results") — flag non-discriminating assertions, flaky high-variance evals, time/token tradeoffs.
9. Launch viewer: `nohup python <skill-creator-path>/eval-viewer/generate_review.py <workspace>/iteration-N --skill-name "my-skill" --benchmark <workspace>/iteration-N/benchmark.json > /dev/null 2>&1 & VIEWER_PID=$!`; for iteration ≥2 add `--previous-workspace <workspace>/iteration-<N-1>`. Headless/Cowork ⇒ `--static <output_path>` writes standalone HTML; feedback arrives as a downloaded `feedback.json`.
10. Direct the user: "Outputs" tab (per-test-case prompt, rendered output, collapsible Previous Output/Formal Grades, auto-saving feedback box, Previous Feedback) and "Benchmark" tab (stats + analyst notes); arrow-key navigation; "Submit All Reviews" persists `feedback.json`.
11. On completion, read `feedback.json` (`reviews[{run_id, feedback, timestamp}], status:"complete"`); empty feedback = approval — concentrate fixes on complained-about cases. Kill `$VIEWER_PID`.

**Phase 6 — Improve the Skill.** Four levers: (1) **Generalize** — the skill must serve millions of unseen prompts, so trade fiddly overfit patches for different metaphors/working patterns; (2) **Keep lean** — prune dead weight, and read transcripts (not just outputs) to excise instructions that cause unproductive churn; (3) **Explain the why** — LLMs respond better to reasoned instructions than rigid structures; treat ALL-CAPS ALWAYS/NEVER as a refactor signal; (4) **Bundle repeated work** — if every test run independently wrote e.g. `create_docx.py`, promote it into `scripts/`. Mull deeply; draft, then revise with fresh eyes.

**Phase 7 — Iteration Loop.** Apply improvements → rerun all test cases into `iteration-<N+1>/` (baselines included; new-skill baseline stays `without_skill`, improvement baseline is judgment between original and previous iteration) → relaunch reviewer with `--previous-workspace` → await user review → repeat until the user is happy, feedback is entirely empty, or progress stalls.

**Phase 8 — Advanced Blind Comparison (optional).** For rigorous "is v2 actually better?" questions: give two anonymized outputs (A/B) to an independent comparator agent (`agents/comparator.md`), then unblind and analyze why the winner won (`agents/analyzer.md`). Requires subagents; most users won't need it.

**Phase 9 — Description Optimization.**
1. Generate ~20 trigger-eval queries (8–10 should-trigger, 8–10 should-not) saved as `[{"query": ..., "should_trigger": bool}]`. Queries must be realistic Claude Code/Claude.ai utterances: concrete file paths, personal context, column names, company names, URLs, backstory, lowercase/casual/typos, varied lengths, edge-case-heavy. Should-trigger coverage spans formal/casual phrasings, unnamed-skill cases, uncommon uses, competitive contexts. Should-not-trigger focuses on near-misses sharing keywords but needing something else — never obviously irrelevant negatives ("Write a fibonacci function" tests nothing). Queries must be substantive enough that consulting a skill would genuinely help (simple one-step queries won't trigger regardless of description quality).
2. User review via `assets/eval_review.html`: substitute `__EVAL_DATA_PLACEHOLDER__` (raw JS assignment), `__SKILL_NAME_PLACEHOLDER__`, `__SKILL_DESCRIPTION_PLACEHOLDER__`; write to `/tmp/eval_review_<skill>.html` and open; user edits/toggles/adds/deletes then clicks "Export Eval Set"; retrieve freshest `~/Downloads/eval_set*.json`.
3. Background loop: `python -m scripts.run_loop --eval-set <path> --skill-path <path> --model <model-id-powering-this-session> --max-iterations 5 --verbose`. The loop stratifies 60% train / 40% held-out test, evaluates each query 3× for reliable trigger rate, calls Claude to propose improved descriptions from failures (generalizing, not enumerating), re-evaluates on both splits, iterates ≤5×, streams a live auto-refreshing HTML report, and selects `best_description` by **test** score to avoid overfitting. Periodically tail output for user updates.
4. Apply `best_description` to SKILL.md frontmatter; show before/after with scores.

**Phase 10 — Package & Present.** If a file-presentation tool exists (`present_files` / `SendUserFile`): `python -m scripts.package_skill <path/to/skill-folder>` and send the resulting `.skill` — its card shows a **Save skill** button (org permitting) that installs into the user's profile. Skip if no such tool.

**Environment adaptations.** *Claude.ai:* no subagents ⇒ execute each test personally by reading and following the SKILL.md, sequentially; skip baselines and quantitative benchmarking; if no browser/display, present results inline and point users to saved files; skip description optimization and blind comparison; packaging still works. *Cowork:* subagents available (serial fallback on severe timeouts); no display ⇒ `--static` HTML plus a clickable link; always generate the viewer before self-assessment; feedback arrives via download; description optimization works (subprocess `claude -p`) but runs last.

### 5. Supporting Files, Scripts & Internal Assets Breakdown

| File Name | File Type | Purpose & Exact Working Mechanism |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `LICENSE.txt` | Legal | Full Apache License 2.0 text governing redistribution, contributions, patent grant, and warranty disclaimer for the skill. |
| `SKILL.md` | Markdown + YAML frontmatter | The orchestrating instruction document: lifecycle philosophy, communication calibration, creation guide (anatomy, progressive disclosure, writing patterns/style), test-run protocol, grading/aggregation/viewer commands, improvement doctrine, blind comparison, description optimization, environment-specific overrides, and reference-file index. |
| `agents/grader.md` | Agent spec (Markdown) | Grader subagent contract. Inputs: `expectations`, `transcript_path`, `outputs_dir`. Eight-step process: read transcript fully → inspect actual output files (use provided inspection tools for non-text; don't trust transcript claims alone) → verdict per assertion (PASS requires genuine-substance evidence; superficial/coincidental satisfaction FAILS; burden of proof on expectation; no partial credit) → extract & verify implicit claims typed factual/process/quality → read optional `{outputs_dir}/user_notes.md` → critique the evals themselves (flag trivially-passable assertions, uncovered important outcomes, unverifiable checks — high bar, "good catch" standard) → write `{outputs_dir}/../grading.json` → merge `metrics.json` + `timing.json`. Output schema: `expectations[{text, passed, evidence}]`, `summary{passed, failed, total, pass_rate}`, `execution_metrics`, `timing`, `claims[]`, `user_notes_summary{uncertainties, needs_review, workarounds}`, optional `eval_feedback{suggestions[{assertion?, reason}], overall}`. |
| `agents/comparator.md` | Agent spec (Markdown) | Blind A/B judge. Receives `output_a_path`, `output_b_path`, `eval_prompt`, optional `expectations`; must stay blind to provenance. Builds an adapted two-dimension rubric — Content (correctness/completeness/accuracy) and Structure (organization/formatting/usability), each criterion scored 1–5 — computes dimension averages and an overall 1–10 score, treats assertion pass-rates as secondary evidence, and picks a winner by priority rubric → assertions → rare TIE. Emits `comparison.json` with `winner`, `reasoning`, `rubric{A,B}`, `output_quality{score, strengths, weaknesses}`, optional `expectation_results`. |
| `agents/analyzer.md` | Agent spec (Markdown, dual-role) | **Role 1 — Post-hoc (after blind comparison):** unblinds results; reads both skills and transcripts; compares structural differences and execution patterns; scores instruction-following 1–10 per side; lists winner strengths / loser weaknesses with quotes; emits prioritized `improvement_suggestions` categorized as `instructions|tools|examples|error_handling|structure|references` with `high|medium|low` impact priorities; writes `analysis.json` including `transcript_insights`. Guidelines: specific quotes, actionable changes, causation over correlation, generalization check. **Role 2 — Benchmark analysis:** inputs `benchmark_data_path`, `skill_path`, `output_path`; detects per-assertion patterns (always-pass = non-discriminating, always-fail = broken, skill-only-pass = value, skill-only-fail = harm, variable = flaky), cross-eval difficulty/variance patterns, and resource anomalies (time/tokens/tool_calls outliers); writes a JSON **array of strings**; forbidden from suggesting improvements, subjective judgments, speculation, or repeating aggregates. |
| `assets/eval_review.html` | HTML/JS template | Trigger-eval-set review UI. Three placeholders: `__EVAL_DATA_PLACEHOLDER__` (JSON array injected as a raw JS variable), `__SKILL_NAME_PLACEHOLDER__`, `__SKILL_DESCRIPTION_PLACEHOLDER__`. Renders an editable table sorted should-trigger-first with section headers; each row has a textarea query editor, a toggle switch for `should_trigger`, and delete; "+ Add Query" appends; live summary counts; "Export Eval Set" filters blank queries and downloads `eval_set.json` via Blob/objectURL. |
| `eval-viewer/generate_review.py` | Python CLI (stdlib-only) | Builds and serves (or statically writes) the qualitative review page. **CLI:** `python generate_review.py <workspace> [--port/-p PORT=3117] [--skill-name/-n NAME] [--previous-workspace PATH] [--benchmark PATH] [--static/-s PATH]`. Recursively discovers runs (directories containing `outputs/`, skipping `node_modules/.git/__pycache__/skill/inputs`), resolves prompts from `eval_metadata.json` (run-dir then parent) falling back to a `## Eval Prompt` regex in `transcript.md`, and embeds every output file as text / base64 image / PDF data-URI / XLSX base64 (SheetJS-rendered) / binary download, excluding metadata files `{transcript.md, user_notes.md, metrics.json}`. Loads `grading.json` per run and prior-iteration feedback+outputs when `--previous-workspace` is given. Injects everything into `viewer.html` at the `/*__EMBEDDED_DATA__*/` marker. Server mode kills any lsof-detected occupant of the port (falls back to a free port), regenerates HTML on every `GET /` so refreshes pick up new outputs, exposes `GET/POST /api/feedback` (POST validates a `reviews` key and writes `feedback.json`), suppresses request logs, and auto-opens the browser. `--static` exits after writing a standalone HTML file. |
| `eval-viewer/viewer.html` | HTML/JS template | The viewer shell consuming `EMBEDDED_DATA`. Header with progress counter; tab bar appears only when benchmark data exists (**Outputs** / **Benchmark**). Outputs panel: config badge derived from run id (`with_skill|without_skill|new_skill|old_skill`; baselines amber, primary blue), prompt block, per-file output cards (text `<pre>`, image, PDF iframe, XLSX via SheetJS `sheet_to_html` with per-sheet labels, binary download link), collapsible **Previous Output**, collapsible **Formal Grades** (pass-rate badge colored ≥80% green / ≥50% neutral / else red, per-assertion ✓/✗ with evidence), auto-saving feedback textarea (800 ms debounce; server POST or "Will download on submit"), and Previous Feedback callout. Benchmark panel renders metadata line, summary table (mean ± stddev, delta coloring), per-eval breakdown tables grouped by configuration with Avg rows, per-assertion cross-config grids with hover-title evidence, and Analysis Notes. Nav via buttons/arrow keys (textarea-safe), visited-run tracking promotes "Submit All Reviews", done overlay, toast. ### 6. Inputs, Outputs & Produced Artifacts

- **Expected Inputs:**
  - Natural-language intent: a target capability description, an existing conversation to distill, or a path to an existing skill directory (`<skill-path>/SKILL.md` + resources).
  - User answers to the four intent questions (purpose, trigger contexts, output format, test-case appetite) plus interview details: edge cases, I/O formats, example files, success criteria, dependencies.
  - Test prompts (2–3 authored per iteration) and optional input fixture files referenced by `evals[].files`.
  - Optional MCP connections / subagent capacity for parallel research and run execution.
  - For description optimization: a reviewed trigger-eval set JSON (`[{"query", "should_trigger"}]`, ~20 items) exported from the review UI, and the current session's model ID (so trigger tests match the user's live experience).
  - Environment capabilities: presence of subagents, browser/display, `claude` CLI, and a file-presentation tool determine which branches execute.

- **Produced Outputs / Artifacts:**
  - A drafted or revised skill: `<skill-name>/SKILL.md` (pushy description, ≤1024 chars) plus any `scripts/`, `references/`, `assets/` bundles.
  - `evals/evals.json` — test registry, initially prompt-only, later augmented with `expectations`.
  - Evaluation workspace `<skill-name>-workspace/` (sibling of the skill dir) containing per iteration: `iteration-N/eval-<descriptive-name>/` with `eval_metadata.json` (`eval_id`, `eval_name`, `prompt`, `assertions`), paired run dirs `with_skill/outputs/` + `without_skill/outputs/` (or `old_skill/` when snapshot-improving, alongside `skill-snapshot/`), per-run `timing.json` (`total_tokens`, `duration_ms`, `total_duration_seconds`), and `grading.json` (`expectations[text/passed/evidence]`, `summary`, `execution_metrics`, `timing`, `claims`, `user_notes_summary`, optional `eval_feedback`).
  - `iteration-N/benchmark.json` + `benchmark.md` — per-configuration pass_rate/time/tokens with mean ± stddev/min/max and signed deltas, per-run expectations, and analyzer notes.
  - The eval viewer: a served localhost page (default port 3117) or a standalone HTML file (`--static`), rendering outputs, prior-iteration context, formal grades, and the benchmark tab.
  - `feedback.json` in the workspace — `{reviews:[{run_id, feedback, timestamp}], status:"complete"}` driving the next revision.
  - Trigger-optimization artifacts: `eval_set.json`, live/final optimization reports (HTML), optional `results-<timestamp>/` with `results.json`, `report.html`, and `logs/improve_iter_*.json` transcripts, culminating in `best_description` applied to the skill frontmatter.
  - Final deliverable: `<skill-name>.skill` zip archive (validator-approved, build-artifact-free), presented via file-delivery tooling when available.

### 7. Ecosystem Coordination & Related Skills

- **Pairs With:**
  - **The skill under development** — skill-creator wraps, exercises, and refines any target skill; the target's own domain skills/MCPs may be exercised inside test runs.
  - **Subagent infrastructure** — grader, comparator, and analyzer personas (`agents/*.md`) are spawned as specialized subagents; test-case executors run as parallel with-skill/baseline subagents.
  - **MCP servers** — leveraged during the Interview & Research phase for doc lookup, similar-skill discovery, and best-practice gathering.
  - **Claude Code CLI (`claude -p`)** — the execution substrate for trigger-rate evaluation and description proposal in the optimization loop.
  - **File-presentation tooling** (`present_files` / `SendUserFile`) — delivers the packaged `.skill` whose card integrates the org-gated **Save skill** installation flow.
  - **TodoList facility** — mandated checkpoint tracking (especially the Cowork-specific viewer reminder).

- **Conflicts / Disambiguation:**
  - **vs. `/skill-test` (and any other testing skill):** hard conflict — skill-creator's run/grade/aggregate/viewer pipeline replaces it entirely; invoking `/skill-test` mid-workflow is explicitly prohibited.
  - **vs. generic code-testing/CI skills:** skill-creator evaluates *behavioral skill quality* (does the skill cause better agent outputs?) via paired with-skill/baseline subagent runs and human review — not unit/integration correctness of application code.
  - **vs. prompt-engineering helpers:** skill-creator targets the skill artifact (frontmatter-triggered, progressively disclosed, resource-bundled) and its *triggering* behavior, not freeform prompt tweaking; description changes are validated empirically against held-out trigger queries.
  - **vs. blind comparison ad-hoc judging:** the built-in comparator/analyzer pair enforces blinding, rubric discipline, and causal attribution; informal eyeballing is reserved for the standard human-review loop.
  - **Self-disambiguation at runtime:** because this skill's description is intentionally broad about "creating/editing/optimizing skills," it should yield to domain-specific creation skills when the user's goal is the domain artifact itself rather than the skill engineering process; conversely, any request mentioning skill evals, benchmarks, variance analysis, or trigger optimization routes here.

## 44. `skill-stocktake`

- **Canonical Directory:** `.agents/skills/skill-stocktake/`
- **Author & Version:** ECC (declared via `metadata.origin: ECC` in SKILL.md frontmatter); no explicit version field — treated as Workspace Built-in
- **Primary Domain & Category:** Meta-skill / Agent Tooling Governance — skill-inventory auditing, lifecycle curation (Keep / Improve / Update / Retire / Merge), and knowledge-base hygiene automation

### 1. Executive Summary & Core Working Principle

`skill-stocktake` is a slash command (`/skill-stocktake`) that turns inventory-management discipline onto the AI agent's own capability library. Its core mental model is a **warehouse stocktake**: every skill file (`SKILL.md`) is an asset with a location, a last-modified timestamp, an observed usage frequency, and a fitness-for-purpose verdict. Rather than letting the skill library grow unbounded and stale, this skill periodically reconciles what exists on disk against what is actually valuable, current, and non-duplicative.

Three principles define its design:

1. **Incremental economics via a timestamp ledger.** A persistent cache (`results.json`) records `evaluated_at` plus a per-skill verdict and `mtime`. On subsequent runs, the Quick Scan mode diffs current file mtimes against `evaluated_at`, so only changed or newly added skills are re-evaluated — reducing a 20–30 minute full review to 5–10 minutes.
2. **Holistic AI judgment, not a numeric rubric.** Evaluation is delegated to a general-purpose subagent that applies a fixed four-item checklist (overlap, memory-file overlap, technical freshness, usage frequency) and renders one of five verdicts (`Keep`, `Improve`, `Update`, `Retire`, `Merge into [X]`). Guiding dimensions are actionability, scope fit, uniqueness, and currency — deliberately qualitative.
3. **Decision-enabling evidence over lazy labels.** Every verdict's `reason` must be self-contained enough for a future reader to act on it without re-doing the analysis ("unchanged", "Superseded", "Too long" are explicitly banned patterns). Destructive outcomes (Retire/Merge/archive/delete) are proposals only until the user explicitly confirms.

The result is a closed audit loop: **scan → batch-evaluate via subagent → persist with a true UTC timestamp → summarize → consolidate with human sign-off**, with resume support for interrupted batches.

### 2. When to Use (Positive Triggers) vs. When NOT to Use (Negative Triggers)

- **Positive Triggers:**
  - Verbatim activation trigger from the skill description: *"Use when auditing Claude skills and commands for quality."*
  - User invokes `/skill-stocktake` — runs **Quick Scan** by default when `~/.claude/skills/skill-stocktake/results.json` exists.
  - User invokes `/skill-stocktake full`, or `results.json` is absent — runs the **Full Stocktake** (all four phases, 20–30 min).
  - After bulk-adding, importing, or auto-extracting a batch of new skills and needing a quality gate before they enter regular rotation.
  - Periodic hygiene passes: detecting stale technical references (outdated CLI flags/APIs), overlapping skills, or skills whose value is already covered by `MEMORY.md` / `CLAUDE.md`.
  - When preparing to compress `MEMORY.md` (Phase 4 checks its line count and proposes compression if >100 lines).
  - After an interrupted run: a `results.json` with `"status": "in_progress"` triggers resume-from-first-unevaluated-skill behavior.

- **Negative Triggers / Anti-Patterns:**
  - **Do NOT** use this to audit application/source code, PRs, or feature implementations — it exclusively targets skill/command markdown files under `~/.claude/skills/` and `{cwd}/.claude/skills/`. Code-review concerns belong to review-oriented skills (e.g., `receiving-code-review`, `ponytail-review` in the same inventory).
  - **Do NOT** use it as a skill *authoring* tool — it evaluates existing inventory; creation of new skills is out of scope.
  - **Do NOT** perform archive/delete/merge file operations without explicit user confirmation — the skill mandates presenting justification first.
  - **Do NOT** set `SKILL_STOCKTAKE_GLOBAL_DIR` or `SKILL_STOCKTAKE_PROJECT_DIR` in production — these are testing-only overrides intended for bats tests.
  - **Do NOT** fabricate timestamps: never write a date-only approximation like `T00:00:00Z` into `evaluated_at`.
  - **Do NOT** expect numeric scores — there is no scoring rubric; forcing quantitative ranking misuses the design.
  - **Do NOT** branch verdicts by skill origin (ECC vs. self-authored vs. auto-extracted) — evaluation is intentionally blind.
  - If Quick Scan's diff returns `[]`, stop and report "No changes since last run." — do not force a re-evaluation.

### 3. Hard Execution Gates & Invariants

1. **User-confirmation gate on destruction:** Archive/delete operations (and executing Retire/Merge verdicts) always require explicit user confirmation. Phase 4 must present per-file justification — the specific problem found, the covering alternative, and removal impact (dependent skills, `MEMORY.md` references, affected workflows) — *before* asking.
2. **True-UTC timestamp invariant:** `evaluated_at` must be obtained via `date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ` at evaluation completion. Date-only approximations (e.g., `T00:00:00Z`) are forbidden because Quick Scan relies on ISO 8601 string comparison of mtimes against this value.
3. **Reason-quality invariant:** Each `reason` must be self-contained and decision-enabling. Banned: bare `"unchanged"`, `"Superseded"`, `"Overlaps with X"`, `"Too long"`. Required shape: for **Retire** — (1) specific defect, (2) what covers the need instead; for **Merge** — named target plus what content to integrate; for **Improve** — section, action, and target size; for **Keep** on mtime-only Quick Scan changes — restate the original rationale.
4. **Path-disclosure invariant:** At the start of Phase 1, the command must explicitly list which paths were found and scanned (e.g., `✓ ~/.claude/skills/ (17 files)` / `✗ {cwd}/.claude/skills/ (not found — global skills only)`).
5. **Batch-chunking & checkpoint invariant:** Process ~20 skills per subagent invocation; after each chunk, persist intermediate results to `results.json` with `"status": "in_progress"`. On startup, if `in_progress` is detected, resume from the first unevaluated skill rather than restarting.
6. **Early-exit gate:** If `quick-diff.sh` outputs `[]`, report "No changes since last run." and halt — no evaluation phase is entered.
7. **Script-level fail-fast validation:** `quick-diff.sh` exits 1 if `RESULTS_JSON` is missing/unreadable, and exits 1 if `evaluated_at` fails the strict regex `^[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}T[0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}Z$` (preventing unpredictable comparisons against `null`/malformed values). `save-results.sh` exits 1 if stdin is not valid JSON (`jq empty`) and if `RESULTS_JSON` argument is empty.
8. **Safety invariants inside scripts:** temp dirs/files are created via `mktemp` with `trap`-based cleanup (collision-safe, injection-resistant — `$tmpdir` is never embedded in quoted strings); known-path lookup uses exact whole-line matching (`grep -qxF` / awk `$2 == f`) to prevent substring false-positives such as `python-patterns` matching `python-patterns-v2`; a defense-in-depth warning fires if a skills-dir argument exists but does not look like a `.claude/skills*` path.
9. **Blind-evaluation invariant:** The identical checklist applies to all skills regardless of origin; no verdict branching by provenance.

### 4. Step-by-Step Execution Workflow & Pipeline

**Step 0 — Mode selection.** Check for `~/.claude/skills/skill-stocktake/results.json`. Present → Quick Scan (default, 5–10 min). Absent, or user passed `/skill-stocktake full` → Full Stocktake (20–30 min). If `results.json` carries `"status": "in_progress"`, resume the interrupted batch instead of starting fresh.

**Path A — Quick Scan Flow (incremental):**
1. Read `~/.claude/skills/skill-stocktake/results.json`.
2. Run `bash ~/.claude/skills/skill-stocktake/scripts/quick-diff.sh ~/.claude/skills/skill-stocktake/results.json` (project dir auto-detected from `$PWD/.claude/skills`; pass explicitly only if needed). The script emits a JSON array of changed/new files (`{path, mtime, is_new}`).
3. **Gate:** if output is `[]` → report "No changes since last run." and stop.
4. Re-evaluate only the changed/new files using the same Phase 2 checklist and verdict criteria.
5. Carry forward unchanged skills' previous verdicts from prior results.
6. Output only the diff.
7. Persist via `bash .../save-results.sh ~/.claude/skills/skill-stocktake/results.json <<< "$EVAL_RESULTS"` (script stamps a fresh UTC `evaluated_at` and merges `.skills`, new entries overriding old).

**Path B — Full Stocktake Flow:**

- **Phase 1 — Inventory:** Run `bash ~/.claude/skills/skill-stocktake/scripts/scan.sh`. The script enumerates `*.md` files under `~/.claude/skills/` and `{cwd}/.claude/skills/`, extracts `name`/`description` frontmatter, records UTC mtimes, and counts Read-tool observations over 7-day and 30-day windows. Present the mandatory scan-summary disclosure plus the inventory table (`| Skill | 7d use | 30d use | Description |`).
- **Phase 2 — Quality Evaluation:** Launch an Agent tool subagent (`subagent_type="general-purpose"`) with a prompt embedding `[INVENTORY]` and `[CHECKLIST]`, requesting per-skill JSON `{ "verdict": "Keep"|"Improve"|"Update"|"Retire"|"Merge into [X]", "reason": "..." }`. The subagent reads each skill and applies the checklist: (a) content overlap with other skills; (b) overlap with `MEMORY.md` / `CLAUDE.md`; (c) freshness of technical references (use WebSearch when tool names / CLI flags / APIs appear); (d) usage frequency. Verdict semantics: **Keep** = useful and current; **Improve** = worth keeping with specific fixes needed; **Update** = referenced technology outdated (verify via WebSearch); **Retire** = low quality/stale/cost-asymmetric; **Merge into [X]** = substantial overlap, target named. Chunk ~20 skills per invocation, checkpointing `results.json` (`status: "in_progress"`) after each chunk; on completion set `status: "completed"`.
- **Phase 3 — Summary Table:** Render `| Skill | 7d use | Verdict | Reason |` across the full inventory.
- **Phase 4 — Consolidation:** (1) For Retire/Merge, present detailed per-file justification (problem found, covering alternative, removal impact) and obtain user confirmation before any archive/delete; (2) for Improve, present concrete change proposals with rationale (e.g., "trim 430→200 lines because sections X/Y duplicate python-patterns") — the user decides whether to act; (3) for Update, present refreshed content with sources checked; (4) check `MEMORY.md` line count and propose compression if it exceeds 100 lines.

### 5. Supporting Files, Scripts & Internal Assets Breakdown

| File Name | File Type | Purpose & Exact Working Mechanism |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `SKILL.md` | Markdown skill definition (YAML frontmatter + body) | Canonical contract: mode-selection rules, scope table, Quick Scan 7-step flow, Full Stocktake Phases 1–4, evaluation checklist, verdict taxonomy, reason-quality bad/good exemplars, and the `results.json` schema. Frontmatter: `name: skill-stocktake`, `metadata.origin: ECC`. |
| `scripts/scan.sh` | Bash CLI (inventory enumerator) | **Usage:** `scan.sh [CWD_SKILLS_DIR]` (defaults to `$PWD/.claude/skills`). Scans global dir `${SKILL_STOCKTAKE_GLOBAL_DIR:-$HOME/.claude/skills}` plus the project dir; for each `*.md` it extracts `name`/`description` via an awk frontmatter parser (single-line quoted/unquoted values only — no multi-line YAML blocks/nested keys), captures UTC mtime (`date -u -r`), and computes `use_7d`/`use_30d` by aggregating Read-tool events from `${SKILL_STOCKTAKE_OBSERVATIONS:-$HOME/.claude/observations.jsonl}` in two pre-aggregated passes (O(n+m) jq calls instead of per-file). Cross-platform dates via `date -v-Nd` (BSD) fallback `date -d "N days ago"` (GNU). Paths are home-collapsed to `~/…`. **Output:** `{scan_summary:{global:{found,count},project:{found,path,count}},skills:[{path,name,description,use_7d,use_30d,mtime}]}`; emits `[]` for empty dirs. |
| `scripts/quick-diff.sh` | Bash CLI (incremental differ) | **Usage:** `quick-diff.sh RESULTS_JSON [CWD_SKILLS_DIR]`. Reads `.evaluated_at`, hard-fails (exit 1) on missing file or on values not matching `^[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}T[0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}Z$`. Pre-extracts `.skills[].path` into a known-paths set for O(1) per-file lookup. Walks sorted `*.md` files; for known paths emits an entry only when `mtime > evaluated_at` (safe ISO-string compare); unknown paths always emit with `is_new:true`. Matching is exact whole-line (`grep -qxF`) to avoid substring collisions between similarly named skills. **Output:** JSON array `[{path,mtime,is_new}]` to stdout, `[]` when clean. |
| `scripts/save-results.sh` | Bash CLI (merge/persist writer) | **Usage:** `save-results.sh RESULTS_JSON <<< "$EVAL_JSON"`. The provided sample shows a completed full-mode run over 33 skills (Windows-style `A:/billsplit/.agents/skills/...` paths), all verdict `Keep`. This file is simultaneously the Quick Scan diff baseline and the batch-resume checkpoint. |

### 6. Inputs, Outputs & Produced Artifacts

- **Expected Inputs:**
  - Slash-command invocation: `/skill-stocktake` (Quick Scan default) or `/skill-stocktake full`.
  - Existing `~/.claude/skills/skill-stocktake/results.json` (mode selector, diff baseline, resume checkpoint).

## 45. `slack-gif-creator`

- **Canonical Directory:** `.agents/skills/slack-gif-creator/`
- **Author & Version:** Anthropic, PBC (Copyright 2026, per `LICENSE.txt`; Apache License 2.0). No explicit version field is present in the SKILL.md frontmatter — treat as **Workspace Built-in**.
- **Primary Domain & Category:** Creative Media Generation / Animation Tooling. Python-based programmatic GIF synthesis, optimization, and validation targeted specifically at Slack's emoji and message GIF constraints.

### 1. Executive Summary & Core Working Principle

`slack-gif-creator` is a **knowledge-plus-utilities** skill for producing animated GIFs that conform to Slack's technical constraints. Its philosophy is deliberately *not* to be a template library: it provides the **knowledge** (Slack's dimension/FPS/color/duration limits and a catalog of animation concepts), the **utilities** (a `GIFBuilder` assembly pipeline, validators, easing functions, and frame-composition helpers), and the **flexibility** (the agent writes the actual animation logic itself using PIL primitives).

**Core mental model:** A GIF is a list of RGB frames generated frame-by-frame in a loop. For each frame index `i`, the agent computes a progress value `t = i / (num_frames - 1)`, optionally passes it through an easing function for natural motion, draws the scene with `PIL.ImageDraw` primitives (ellipses, polygons, lines, rectangles), and hands the frame to `GIFBuilder`. On `save()`, the builder quantizes colors using a **global palette** derived from sampled frames (better cross-frame compression), optionally deduplicates near-identical frames, applies emoji-specific downsizing, and writes the file via `imageio` with infinite looping. A validator then confirms Slack-readiness.

**Fundamental objective:** Turn a natural-language request ("make me a GIF of X doing Y for Slack") into a polished, size-optimized, looping `.gif` that passes Slack's constraints — with graphics that look hand-crafted (thick outlines, gradients, layered shapes, glows) rather than placeholder-quality.

**Explicit non-goals:** No emoji-font rendering (unreliable across platforms), no pre-packaged graphics library, no rigid animation templates.

### 2. When to Use (Positive Triggers) vs. When NOT to Use (Negative Triggers)

- **Positive Triggers:**
  - Verbatim request pattern: *"make me a GIF of X doing Y for Slack"* — the canonical activation phrase in the skill description.
  - Any request for an **animated Slack emoji GIF** (target: 128×128, under 3 seconds).
  - Any request for an **animated Slack message GIF** (target: 480×480).
  - *"Animate this"* / *"split this into frames"* — when a user uploads an image and wants it used **directly** as animation source material.
  - *"Make something like this"* — when an uploaded image should be used as **inspiration** for colors/style while drawing from scratch.
  - Requests to **shrink an existing GIF's file size** (triggers the Optimization Strategies section: fewer frames/colors, deduplication, emoji mode).
  - Requests involving animation effects: shake/vibrate, pulse/heartbeat, bounce, spin/rotate, fade in/out, slide, zoom, explode/particle burst — or combinations thereof (e.g., bouncing + rotating).

- **Negative Triggers / Anti-Patterns:**
  - **Static images** with no animation component — use a general image-generation/editing skill instead.
  - **Video formats** (MP4, WebM, MOV) — this skill only emits GIF; do not promise video output.
  - **Non-Slack GIF targets** where Slack's constraints (128×128 emoji, 480×480 message) don't apply — the skill can still build the GIF, but its optimization defaults and validators are Slack-specific.
  - **Emoji/text rendering via emoji fonts** — explicitly forbidden (unreliable across platforms). Draw shapes with PIL primitives or use `draw_text` with Pillow's default font instead.
  - **Expectation of pre-made graphics** — the skill ships no sticker/clipart library; do not assume assets exist.
  - **Unsolicited file-size optimization** — optimization strategies must only be applied *when the user asks to make the file smaller*.

### 3. Hard Execution Gates & Invariants

This skill contains no `<HARD-GATE>` XML tags, but enforces the following mandatory invariants and behavioral halts:

1. **Slack parameter invariants (must hold for output):**
   - Emoji GIFs: **128×128** dimensions, duration **under 3 seconds**.
   - Message GIFs: **480×480** dimensions.
   - FPS within **10–30** (lower = smaller file); colors within **48–128** (fewer = smaller file).
2. **No emoji fonts.** Never render emoji glyphs via system fonts; draw graphics with PIL primitives.
3. **No assumed assets.** Never assume pre-packaged graphics exist inside the skill; all art is drawn programmatically or derived from user uploads.
4. **Line-width floor:** outlines and lines must use `width=2` or higher; `width=1` is prohibited as visually unacceptable ("choppy and amateurish").
5. **Optimization gating:** file-size reduction strategies (fewer frames, `num_colors=48`, dimension reduction, `remove_duplicates=True`, `optimize_for_emoji=True`) are applied **only when the user explicitly asks for a smaller file**.
6. **`GIFBuilder.save()` hard failure:** raises `ValueError("No frames to save...")` if `save()` is called before any frame is added — frames must be added first.
7. **Emoji-mode auto-overrides in `save()`:** when `optimize_for_emoji=True`, the builder unconditionally (a) resizes frames >128px down to 128×128 (LANCZOS), (b) caps `num_colors` at 48, and (c) subsamples frames down to ~12 if more exist. These overrides cannot be opted out of within emoji mode.
8. **Validation before delivery:** output should be checked with `validate_gif()` / `is_slack_ready()`; emoji dimension pass requires a square image with 64 ≤ side ≤ 128 (128×128 flagged "optimal"); message GIFs require aspect ratio ≤ 2.0 and 320 ≤ min(side) ≤ 640.
9. **Upload interpretation gate:** for user-uploaded images, the agent must first decide — based on the request — whether the image is to be **used directly** or used **as inspiration only**.

### 4. Step-by-Step Execution Workflow & Pipeline

1. **Request parsing & target classification.** Determine whether the deliverable is a Slack **emoji GIF** (128×128, <3s) or a **message GIF** (480×480). If a user image was uploaded, classify it as "use directly" vs. "inspiration."
2. **Environment preparation.** Ensure dependencies are installed: `pip install pillow imageio numpy` (versions pinned in `requirements.txt`: `pillow>=10.0.0`, `imageio>=2.31.0`, `imageio-ffmpeg>=0.4.9`, `numpy>=1.24.0`).
3. **Builder instantiation.** `builder = GIFBuilder(width=..., height=..., fps=...)` — defaults are 480×480 @ 15 fps; use 128×128 @ ~10 fps for emoji.
4. **Frame generation loop.** For `i in range(num_frames)`:
   - Compute progress `t = i / (num_frames - 1)`.
   - Create a base frame (`create_blank_frame` or `Image.new('RGB', ...)`, optionally `create_gradient_background`).
   - Compute animated parameters via `interpolate(start, end, t, easing='ease_out'|'bounce_out'|'back_out'|...)` or raw `math.sin`/`math.cos` oscillation for shake/pulse.
   - Draw the scene with `ImageDraw` primitives and helpers (`draw_circle`, `draw_star`, `draw_text`), respecting the width≥2 rule and layering shapes for depth (highlights, rings, glows via larger semi-transparent shapes).
   - `builder.add_frame(frame)` (accepts PIL Images or numpy arrays; auto-converts to RGB and auto-resizes mismatched frames with LANCZOS).
5. **Assembly & optimization.** Call `builder.save(output_path, num_colors=..., optimize_for_emoji=..., remove_duplicates=...)`. Internally this: (a) optionally deduplicates near-identical consecutive frames (similarity threshold 0.9995), (b) applies emoji overrides if requested, (c) builds a **global palette** from up to 5 sampled frames and quantizes all frames against it (method=2, dither=1), (d) writes via `imageio.imwrite` with `duration = 1000/fps` ms per frame and `loop=0` (infinite loop), and (e) prints/returns a metadata dict.
6. **Validation.** Run `validate_gif('out.gif', is_emoji=True/False, verbose=True)` (or the `is_slack_ready()` quick check) to confirm dimensions, inspect size, frame count, duration, and FPS.
7. **Conditional size-reduction pass.** If the user asked for a smaller file (or validation flags a large size), apply optimization strategies: lower FPS/shorter duration → fewer colors (`num_colors=48`) → smaller dimensions → `remove_duplicates=True` → `optimize_for_emoji=True`. Re-save and re-validate.
8. **Delivery.** Report the output path plus the info dict (`size_kb`, `dimensions`, `frame_count`, `fps`, `duration_seconds`, `colors`) to the user.

### 5. Supporting Files, Scripts & Internal Assets Breakdown

| File Name | File Type | Purpose & Exact Working Mechanism |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `SKILL.md` | Markdown (skill manifest + knowledge) | Frontmatter: `name: slack-gif-creator`, `description` (activation triggers), `license: Complete terms in LICENSE.txt`. Body documents Slack requirements (emoji 128×128 / message 480×480; FPS 10–30; colors 48–128; emoji <3s), the core 3-step workflow (build → generate frames → save), drawing guidance (PIL primitives, width≥2, gradients, layering, no emoji fonts), 8 animation concept recipes (shake, pulse, bounce, spin, fade, slide, zoom, particle burst), optimization strategies, and the skill philosophy (knowledge + utilities, no templates/assets). |
| `core/gif_builder.py` | Python module | **`GIFBuilder`** class — the assembly pipeline. `__init__(width=480, height=480, fps=15)`. `add_frame(frame)` accepts numpy arrays or PIL Images, converts to RGB, auto-resizes mismatched frames via `Image.Resampling.LANCZOS`. `add_frames(list)` bulk-adds. `optimize_colors(num_colors=128, use_global_palette=True)` builds a global palette by sampling up to 5 evenly-spaced frames, stacking their pixels into a synthetic ≤512-wide RGB image, calling `quantize(colors=N, method=2)`, then re-quantizing every frame against that palette with `dither=1` (falls back to per-frame quantization for single-frame GIFs). `deduplicate_frames(threshold=0.9995)` drops consecutive frames whose similarity `1 - mean(|diff|)/255` ≥ threshold (0.9995 = only near-identical removed; 0.98 = aggressive). `save(output_path, num_colors=128, optimize_for_emoji=False, remove_duplicates=False)` raises `ValueError` on empty frame list; in emoji mode resizes >128px frames to 128×128, caps colors at 48, subsamples to ~12 frames (`keep_every = len(frames)//12`); writes with `imageio.imwrite(..., duration=1000/fps, loop=0)`; returns dict `{path, size_kb, size_mb, dimensions, frame_count, fps, duration_seconds, colors}` and prints a summary with a large-file warning if >1 MB. `clear()` resets frames. |
| `core/validators.py` | Python module | **Slack compliance checks.** `validate_gif(gif_path, is_emoji=True, verbose=True) -> (bool, dict)`: reads file size, dimensions, frame count (via `img.seek` loop until `EOFError`), duration and FPS from GIF metadata. Emoji rule: pass = square with 64 ≤ side ≤ 128; "optimal" flag only at exactly 128×128. Message rule: aspect ratio ≤ 2.0 AND 320 ≤ min(side) ≤ 640. Returns dict `{file, passes, width, height, size_kb, size_mb, frame_count, duration_seconds, fps, is_emoji, optimal}`; verbose mode prints a report and warns on >5 MB files. `is_slack_ready(gif_path, is_emoji=True, verbose=True) -> bool` is a thin boolean wrapper around `validate_gif`. |
| `core/easing.py` | Python module | **Motion timing library.** Ten core easing functions (quad/cubic variants of `ease_in`/`ease_out`/`ease_in_out`, bounce in/out/in-out, elastic in/out/in-out) plus back-easing family (`ease_back_in`, `ease_back_out`, `ease_back_in_out` with overshoot constant c1=1.70158). `EASING_FUNCTIONS` name→function map includes aliases `anticipate`→`back_in` and `overshoot`→`back_out`; `get_easing(name, default='linear')` does safe lookup. `interpolate(start, end, t, easing='linear')` returns `start + (end-start) * eased(t)` — the primary API for animated parameters. `apply_squash_stretch(base_scale, intensity, direction='vertical'\|'horizontal'\|'both')` computes volume-preserving deformation scales (±0.5·intensity on the crossed axis, ±0.3 both-axis squash). `calculate_arc_motion(start, end, height, t)` returns `(x, y)` along a parabolic arc with peak offset `4·height·t·(1-t)` at midpoint — for natural projectile paths. |
| `core/frame_composer.py` | Python module | **Drawing convenience helpers.** `create_blank_frame(width, height, color=(255,255,255))` → solid RGB PIL Image. `draw_circle(frame, center, radius, fill_color, outline_color, outline_width=1)` → ellipse from center/radius bbox, returns modified frame. `draw_text(frame, text, position, color=(0,0,0), centered=False)` renders with `ImageFont.load_default()` (Pillow default font only; swap-point for custom fonts), with bbox-based centering when `centered=True`. `create_gradient_background(width, height, top_color, bottom_color)` → per-row linear RGB interpolation drawn as horizontal lines. `draw_star(frame, center, size, fill_color, outline_color=None, outline_width=1)` → 10-vertex polygon alternating outer radius `size` and inner radius `size*0.4`, starting at −90° (top point). |
| `requirements.txt` | Pip requirements | Pins runtime dependencies: `pillow>=10.0.0`, `imageio>=2.31.0`, `imageio-ffmpeg>=0.4.9`, `numpy>=1.24.0`. |
| `LICENSE.txt` | Legal text | Apache License 2.0, Copyright 2026 Anthropic, PBC. Governs use, redistribution, and contribution terms for the skill. |

### 6. Inputs, Outputs & Produced Artifacts

- **Expected Inputs:**
  - Natural-language animation request, ideally Slack-scoped (e.g., "make me a GIF of a rocket launching for Slack"); implied choices: emoji vs. message GIF, subject, motion concept(s), duration, mood.
  - Optional **user-uploaded image file** (any PIL-readable format, e.g., `file.png`) to animate directly or to use as style/color inspiration.
  - Optional explicit parameters: output filename/path, dimensions (128×128 or 480×480), FPS (10–30), color count (48–128), frame count, easing preference, and an explicit "make it smaller" optimization request.
  - Runtime dependency availability: `pillow`, `imageio`, `numpy` (installed via `requirements.txt`).

- **Produced Outputs / Artifacts:**
  - A **looping animated `.gif` file** at the user-specified (or agent-chosen) output path — e.g., `output.gif`, `emoji.gif` — written with infinite loop (`loop=0`) and per-frame duration `1000/fps` ms.
  - A **build metadata dict** returned by `GIFBuilder.save()`: `{path, size_kb, size_mb, dimensions, frame_count, fps, duration_seconds, colors}` (also echoed to stdout with a ✓ summary and large-file advisory when >1 MB).
  - A **validation report** from `validate_gif()`: pass/fail boolean plus `{file, passes, width, height, size_kb, size_mb, frame_count, duration_seconds, fps, is_emoji, optimal}`, with verbose console output.
  - Console diagnostics during emoji optimization (resize notice, frame-reduction notice, deduplication count).

### 7. Ecosystem Coordination & Related Skills

- **Pairs With:**
  - A **Python/code-execution skill or environment** — mandatory, since all frame generation, building, and validation happen through Python scripts importing `core.*` modules.
  - **Image intake / file-upload handling skills** — to stage user-uploaded images onto disk where `PIL.Image.open()` can load them for direct animation or style reference.
  - **Slack integration / file-upload skills** — to deliver the finished `.gif` into a Slack workspace (as a custom emoji or a channel message attachment) after validation passes.
  - **Dependency/environment-setup skills** — to install `requirements.txt` (`pillow`, `imageio`, `imageio-ffmpeg`, `numpy`) in fresh workspaces.
  - General **creative/brainstorming skills** — useful for conceiving the animation concept (subject, motion, palette) before the deterministic drawing pipeline runs.

- **Conflicts / Disambiguation:**
  - **vs. static image-generation skills:** this skill animates; hand off to image skills when the user wants a single still frame.
  - **vs. video-creation skills:** this skill emits GIF only — never MP4/WebM; do not invoke video pipelines for "GIF for Slack" requests, and do not use this skill when a video codec is explicitly required.
  - **vs. emoji-font/text-rendering approaches:** this skill forbids emoji-font glyph rendering (cross-platform unreliability); any pictorial content must be drawn with PIL primitives or derived from uploads.
  - **vs. generic GIF encoders:** generic tools lack Slack-specific constraints, global-palette quantization, emoji auto-optimization (128×128 / ≤48 colors / ~12 frames), and the Slack validators — prefer this skill whenever the destination is Slack.
  - **Self-limiting scope:** within its own runs, avoid pulling in template/sticker libraries or assuming bundled assets — the skill's contract is that all graphics are generated programmatically per request.

## 46. `stitch-design-taste`

- **Canonical Directory:** `.agents/skills/stitch-design-taste/`
- **Author & Version:** Workspace Built-in (no explicit author/version declared in SKILL.md frontmatter; only `name` and `description` are present)
- **Primary Domain & Category:** UI/UX Design Systems & Frontend Aesthetics — Semantic design-token generation for Google Stitch AI screen generation (Design Engineering / Anti-Generic UI Standards)

### 1. Executive Summary & Core Working Principle

`stitch-design-taste` is a **semantic design system generator** whose purpose is to produce `DESIGN.md` files that act as the **single source of truth** for prompting Google Stitch to generate premium, non-generic UI screens. Its core mental model is that AI-generated interfaces fail not from lack of capability but from defaulting to recognizable "AI slop" clichés — purple neon gradients, Inter typography, centered heroes, 3-equal-card feature rows, and circular spinners. This skill counters that by encoding an **opinionated, curated aesthetic** as natural-language rules paired with precise values (hex codes, rem values, spring physics constants) that Stitch's AI agent can semantically interpret.

The fundamental objective is twofold:

1. **Translation:** Convert battle-tested anti-slop frontend engineering directives into Stitch's native "Visual Descriptions" language — descriptive, evocative rules ("Deep Charcoal Ink #18181B — Zinc-950 depth, never pure black") rather than raw utility-class jargon ("rounded-xl").
2. **Enforcement via Bans:** The skill treats **anti-patterns as equally important as rules**. A large portion of the design system is an explicit "NEVER DO" blacklist (banned fonts, banned colors, banned layouts, banned copywriting clichés) because removing generic tells is what elevates output to a premium tier.

The bundled reference `DESIGN.md` ("Taste Standard") demonstrates the target output: a gallery-airy, asymmetric, spring-physics-driven interface with calibrated Zinc/Slate neutrals, a single accent color, distinctive sans-serif typography (`Geist`/`Satoshi`/`Outfit`), and hardware-accelerated perpetual micro-motion. It also includes a **Configuration dial system** (Creativity, Density, Variance, Motion Intent, each 1–10) that adapts the strictness of every downstream rule to the project's intended vibe — e.g., Creativity 1–3 yields quiet Notion-like interfaces, while 7–10 yields editorial inline-image typography and dramatic asymmetry.

A critical architectural note: Stitch generates **static screens only**. The motion sections of the generated `DESIGN.md` are therefore **code-phase intent documents** — they specify spring physics (`stiffness: 100, damping: 20`), staggered cascade reveals, and `transform`/`opacity`-only animation rules so that a downstream coding agent (Antigravity, Cursor, etc.) can implement the animations when building the exported design into a live product.

### 2. When to Use (Positive Triggers) vs. When NOT to Use (Negative Triggers)

- **Positive Triggers:**
  - "Generate a DESIGN.md for Google Stitch" / "Create a design system file for Stitch screen generation"
  - "Design a premium landing page / dashboard / SaaS UI that doesn't look AI-generated"
  - "Set up a design language before prompting Stitch" / "I want my Stitch screens to match a curated aesthetic"
  - "Configure Stitch MCP Server integration with Cursor, Antigravity, or Gemini CLI for programmatic design generation"
  - "Ban the AI purple / Inter / generic-startup look from my product UI"
  - Any workflow requiring a semantic, agent-readable design token document with explicit color hex codes, typography stacks, component behaviors, layout grids, motion specs, and anti-pattern lists
  - Projects needing adaptive style dials (Creativity / Density / Variance / Motion Intent) tuned before screen generation

- **Negative Triggers / Anti-Patterns:**
  - **Non-Stitch design workflows:** If generating designs for Figma, plain HTML/CSS handoff, or non-Stitch AI UI tools, use a general frontend design skill instead — this skill's output format is optimized for Stitch's semantic "Visual Descriptions" interpretation.
  - **Implementation/coding tasks:** This skill does not write application code. Once a `DESIGN.md` exists and screens are exported, hand off to a coding agent (Antigravity, Cursor) — the motion section is intent documentation, not implementation.
  - **Neutral/unopinionated design requests:** If the user explicitly wants a "safe," conventional, or brand-mandated design system that violates the bans (e.g., requires Inter, serif dashboards, or centered heroes), this skill's enforced aesthetic conflicts — do not apply it, or override the dials explicitly.
  - **Dashboard serif typography:** Never use this skill's serif allowances (`Fraunces`, `Instrument Serif`) for dashboards or software UIs — serif is categorically banned there regardless of creativity level.
  - **Low-variance centered-hero projects:** If Variance is set ≤ 4, centered Hero layouts become permissible; do not apply the high-variance asymmetric-Hero mandate in those cases.

### 3. Hard Execution Gates & Invariants

The skill enforces the following mandatory, non-negotiable invariants (violations constitute design failure):

- **Single Accent Color Gate:** Maximum **1 accent color per project**, saturation **below 80%**. No mixed warm/cool gray systems within one output — one palette throughout.
- **"AI Purple/Neon" Ban:** Purple/violet neon gradients, purple button glows, and neon gradient aesthetics are strictly BANNED.
- **Pure Black Ban:** `#000000` is never used — only Off-Black, Zinc-950, or Charcoal (`#18181B`).
- **Inter Ban:** `Inter` is BANNED in all premium/creative contexts; force `Geist`, `Outfit`, `Cabinet Grotesk`, or `Satoshi`.
- **Generic Serif Ban:** `Times New Roman`, `Georgia`, `Garamond`, `Palatino` are BANNED. Serif is permitted only via distinctive modern serifs (`Fraunces`, `Gambarino`, `Editorial New`, `Instrument Serif`) and only in editorial/creative contexts — **always banned in dashboards/software UIs**.
- **Layout Invariants:** No overlapping elements (no absolute-positioned content stacking, no z-index layering of content); no "3 equal cards in a row" feature pattern; centered Heroes BANNED when Variance > 4; CSS Grid mandatory over flexbox `calc()` percentage math; `min-h-[100dvh]` mandatory — `h-screen`/`100vh` forbidden (iOS Safari address-bar jump).
- **Responsive Hard Requirement:** Every element must be verified at 375px, 768px, and 1440px (also 390px, 1024px). Mobile (< 768px) collapses to strict single column with **no exceptions**; horizontal scroll on mobile is a **critical failure**; minimum 44px touch targets; body text never below 14px/1rem.
- **Hero Content Bans:** No filler UI text ("Scroll to explore", "Swipe down", scroll arrows, bouncing chevrons); maximum one primary CTA, no secondary "Learn more" links; no redundant micro-copy under headlines.
- **Motion Invariants:** Spring physics only (`stiffness: 100, damping: 20`), no linear easing; animate **only** `transform` and `opacity` — never `top`, `left`, `width`, `height`; grain/noise filters only on fixed, pointer-events-none pseudo-elements; CPU-heavy perpetual animations isolated in microscopic leaf components (never trigger parent re-renders); 60fps minimum target.
- **Loader Invariant:** Skeletal shimmer only — circular spinners are BANNED.
- **Content Authenticity Invariants:** No emojis anywhere (UI, code, alt text); no generic placeholder names ("John Doe", "Acme", "Nexus", "SmartFlow"); no fake round numbers (`99.99%`, `50%`, `1234567`) — use organic data (`47.2%`, `+1 (312) 847-1928`); no AI copywriting clichés ("Elevate", "Seamless", "Unleash", "Next-Gen", "Revolutionize"); no broken Unsplash links — use `picsum.photos/seed/{id}/800/600` or SVG UI Avatars; no uncustomized `shadcn/ui` defaults; no custom mouse cursors; no neon outer glows; no excessive gradient text on large headers; `z-index` reserved only for Navbar/Modal/Overlay layers.
- **High-Density Override Gate:** When Density exceeds Level 7, **all numbers must switch to monospace**.

### 4. Step-by-Step Execution Workflow & Pipeline
